priceSnapshot.note: Against the midday mark of 64,590.8 the tape is DOWN 249.5 points, or 0.39%, and against the 24-hour open of 64,705.6 it is down 0.56%. There was no second reversal. The midday session closed with price mid-box after a violent round trip; the afternoon and evening simply bled lower on decaying range, hour after hour, with no bar making a meaningful attempt at the highs. The hourly sequence tells it plainly: 17:00Z closed 64,619.9, then 64,416.3, 64,445.3, 64,440.4, 64,443.7, 64,354.0, 64,325.8. Six of the last seven hourly closes are lower than the one before, and the 23:00Z hour made the session low at 64,201.0 before a shallow bounce. Session range measured since the midday snapshot (17:45Z onward, 28 fifteen-minute bars): low 64,201.0, high 64,652.1, a 451.1-point band worth 0.32 of a daily ATR against the 0.53 the midday session measured. Range is contracting on every timeframe - daily ATR 1,431.52 from 1,527.54, 4H 515.42 from 543.98, 1H 213.05 from 256.14, 15m 90.59 from 140.15. The single most important fact of the day is that the 06 Aug UTC daily candle is now CLOSED and confirmed: open 64,660.6, high 65,000.0, low 64,172.6, close 64,325.8. That is a 0.52% down day that closed in the bottom 19% of its own range, and it is the sixth consecutive session in which 65,000 was touched or approached and rejected. What it is NOT is a break: 64,325.8 sits 227 points above the UTC daily EMA20 at 64,098.58, so the reclaim structure has now held on a closing basis for an EIGHTH straight day. The whole report is that tension - an intact daily structure sitting on top of a short-term trend that has turned down.

reduceIf.confirmation: A 1H CLOSE below $64,150, unchanged from midday and now far more likely to be tested than it was six hours ago. Price is 191.3 points above this line and the 1H ATR(14) is 213.05, so a single average hour now spans the entire distance. A close below 64,150 does four things at once: it takes out the 64,172.6 low that has held twice, it takes out tonight's 64,201.0 low, it clears the 1h EMA100 at 64,189.33 and it clears the $700,012 liquidation pocket sitting at 64,200. What is left underneath is thin - only $26,870 of realized liquidations in the entire 64,050-64,150 band - and then the UTC daily EMA20 at 64,098.58, the last support of the reclaim thesis and unbroken on closes for eight days. The warnings between spot and the line, in order: the 15m EMA20 at 64,373.57 (already lost), the 64,300 liquidation cluster at $591,330, the 4H EMA20 at 64,251.89 and the 64,201.0 session low.

That level is 689 points away and is not a realistic overnight objective; the honest intermediate repair is a 4H close back above $64,650, which would reclaim the daily EMA50 at 64,639.12 and tonight's 64,652.1 high in one move and would end the lower-highs sequence. Treat 64,650 as the level that cancels the bearish tilt and 65,030 as the level that restores the add.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from ADD to HOLD, the tilt flips from bullish to BEARISH, confidence comes off a third time from 5.4 to 5.1, and a resting overnight stop is now RECOMMENDED at 64,130. The levels themselves are unchanged - 64,150 and 65,030 have been well placed for four sessions running - but everything around them deteriorated. Six things moved and five of them moved the wrong way. FIRST and most important, the 4H MACD histogram finally CROSSED NEGATIVE at -17.38, after five consecutive declining readings of +100.90, +79.52, +56.10, +43.24 and now this. The decay the last three sessions kept flagging has completed; the 4H line at 231.58 is below its signal at 248.96 for the first time in the reclaim. SECOND, the short-term trend is now unambiguously down: price at 64,341.3 is below ALL FOUR 15m EMAs (20 at 64,373.57, 50 at 64,473.44, 100 at 64,518.36, 200 at 64,405.43) and below the 1h EMA20 at 64,511.80 and EMA50 at 64,424.14. THIRD, positioning got worse again - the OKX long/short account ratio is 1.25 at 00:00Z, having peaked at 1.26 through the 21:00-23:00Z hours, up from 1.24 at midday. Retail added longs while price fell 250 points. FOURTH, the ETF bid, which has been the single strongest plank of the bullish case all week, decelerated hard: the 06 Aug Farside row now prints a total of just +9.3M against +244.4M the day before, with HODL at -32.8M. That row is INCOMPLETE - IBIT is still a dash and IBIT was +196.8M yesterday - so this is a warning, not a verdict, and it is the first thing tomorrow's midnight session should re-read. FIFTH, macro tightened for a second straight session: Brent is up another 1.6% from the midday print to 83.71, the dollar index is 99.971 and the US 10-year is 4.678%. Set against all that, exactly one thing improved and it is structural rather than momentum-based: the 06 Aug daily candle CLOSED at 64,325.8, a full 227 points above the daily EMA20 at 64,098.58, making it eight consecutive closes above that line. Open interest also ticked DOWN 0.31% to $2.035B, which is mild deleveraging rather than new longs piling in. So the structure is intact and the momentum is not, the wallet is already 98.8% deployed with 2.44 USDT of cash, and the correct endday stance is to stop adding, hold the core and let a resting stop define the overnight risk.

overnightRisk: The gap to the next report is roughly six and a half hours, from 19:40 COT tonight to the 02:00 COT midnight session, and it spans the thinnest liquidity window of the crypto week - the US afternoon handover into the Asia open with no US equity or bond market to anchor it. Four specific things can move price before anyone looks again. FIRST and most concrete, the incomplete Farside row: IBIT has not reported its 06 Aug flow and every other issuer has, leaving the day at +9.3M. IBIT printed +111.4M, +170.3M and +196.8M on the three preceding days. If it lands positive and large the streak is intact and tonight's fade was noise; if it lands flat or negative the only fundamental leg under this reclaim breaks in the same session that the 4H MACD crossed down, and 64,150 will be tested on the Asia open. That is the single binary that decides tomorrow's midnight call. SECOND, the liquidation geography is now hostile in a way it was not this morning. The $700,012 pocket at 64,200 sits 141 points below spot and the $591,330 pocket at 64,300 sits 41 points below - both directly in the path - while the band from 64,050 to 64,150 holds only $26,870. That is a trapdoor shape: real fuel immediately below, then near-vacuum for a hundred points down to the daily EMA20. A 200-point slip becomes a 400-point slip cheaply in that structure, and it would happen while nobody is watching. THIRD, retail is positioned exactly wrong for it - the long/short account ratio at 1.25-1.26 is the highest reading of the week and it rose while price fell, so the crowded side is the vulnerable side, and realized long liquidations already grew to $1,911,785 against $2,634,056 of shorts, a ratio that has compressed from 6.8-to-1 shorts at the morning read to 1.38-to-1 now. Longs are the ones being carried out at the margin. FOURTH, oil. Brent at 83.71 is up 1.48% on the session and up 1.6% from the midday read, and the US 10-year at 4.678% has been climbing with it; an Asia session that extends the crude move would tighten the rate path further and BTC has correlated negatively with that combination all week. Against these, the structural floor is genuine and worth naming: the daily EMA20 at 64,098.58 has held on closes for eight straight days, the 4H book is still above all four of its EMAs (20 at 64,251.89, 50 at 64,050.23, 100 at 64,054.82, 200 at 63,647.27), volatility is contracting rather than expanding, and 64,172.6 has now been bought twice. The plan follows from that asymmetry rather than from a forecast: a resting stop at 64,130 sits below both tested lows and below the reduce line but ABOVE the daily EMA20, so it exits on a genuine structural break and not on a wick into the 64,200 pocket. Do not add overnight at any price. If price is still between 64,200 and 64,650 at 02:00, nothing has been decided and the midnight session should re-read the IBIT row before anything else.

liquidityMagnet.note: This is deliberately called BALANCED rather than up, and the split is the reason. On raw mass the board still leans overhead: $3,227,629 sits above spot against $1,318,212 below, a 2.45-to-1 skew. But that ratio has compressed sharply from the 3.9-to-1 the midday session measured, and more importantly the geography has inverted at close range. The nearest cluster above is $178,476 at 64,400, only 58.7 points away and thin. The nearest cluster below is $591,330 at 64,300, 41.3 points away and more than three times heavier, with a further $700,012 at 64,200 behind it. So the near-field pull is DOWN and the far-field mass is UP, and calling that a single direction would be dishonest. The practical reading: the heavy overhead pair at 64,800/64,900 marks where a recovery would have to do its hardest work and is 400-560 points away, entirely out of reach on tonight's contracting range, while the two pockets immediately underfoot are live and were both partially paid during this session. The asymmetry that mattered all week - thin below, heavy above - has quietly reversed at the prices that can actually be reached overnight.

calibration.rollingRecord: 28 of 37 resolved sessions helped (76%), across 50 logged rows
calibration.note: The midday call was range with a bullish tilt, a reduce level of 64,150 and an add level of 65,030. Neither fired, and for a fourth consecutive session both levels were well placed: the session low of 64,201.0 stopped 51 points above the reduce line and no 1H bar closed anywhere near it - the lowest completed hourly close was 64,325.8, some 176 points clear - while the 64,652.1 high missed the add level by 378 points, the widest miss of the four. Acting did NOT help this time, which ends the one-session winning run. The midday session deployed 3.00 USDT of spot at 64,590.8 and price is now 249.5 lower at 64,341.3, an unrealised loss of about 0.39% on that tranche. The honest post-mortem is that the midday rationale explicitly argued against waiting for a perfect fill, having watched the morning's 64,100 reserve miss by 72.6 points, and the correction for that lesson overshot: it bought the middle of a 64,172-65,030 box rather than an edge. Both errors are versions of the same mistake, which is treating a level as a certainty in one direction or the other. What the week's four sessions actually establish is that the box has been reliable and the edges have been reliable; it is the middle that keeps costing money. The rolling record moves to 28 of 37 helped.
